proposition.claim:
On pages 59–60, Proposition 10.5 asserts a universal \(C>0\). For real coefficients \(a_i\), an integer \(m\ge1\), a rational prime \(\ell\), and finite \[B=\sum_{i\ge0}|a_i|\ell^{mi},\] small values of \(f(z)=\sum_i a_i z^i\) on \(1,\ell,\ldots,\ell^{m-1}\) are claimed to imply \[|a_i|\le \ell^{(-i+C)m}(B\ell^{-m^2/2}+\epsilon)\quad(i\ge0).
 \tag{R1}\] With both signs of those nodes, the gain is claimed to be \(\ell^{-m^2}\) instead. The exact statements appear in `distribution.tex` lines 105 and 107.

The proof correctly obtains a Cauchy estimate for coefficients of \(q=(f-g)/p\), where \(p\) is the node polynomial and \(g\) is the interpolation polynomial. It then transfers the factor \(\ell^{-im}\) to coefficients of \(f=g+pq\) merely because \(p\) has bounded coefficients (source line 125). This transfer is invalid: the coefficient convolution includes \(b_{i-r}\), whose bound has the additional factor \(\ell^{rm}\).
